newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Nusamba says Busang deal subject to feasibility.
newsitem.headline: Nusamba says Busang deal subject to feasibility.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Indonesia's Nusamba group said on Thursday the Indonesian and American partners of Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd would develop the Busang gold find only if it was economically feasible.

"Nusamba, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc and its Indonesian parters would like to participate in the development of the Busang project only if development is economically feasible," Nia Sarinastiti of public relations company PT Mekurindo, which represents the proposed Busang joint venture company, told Reuters.

She said Nusamba, Freeport and the Indonesian partners' had the right to participate in the Busang project subject to the completion of the evaluation or due diligence work being conducted at the southeast zone of the property.
On February 17, Bre-X issued a statement estimating gold reserves at Busang at 70.95 million ounces.

But Bre-X said in a statement issued in Canada on Wednesday that there appeared to be a "strong possibility" that the potential gold resources on the Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province had been overstated.

"There appears to be a strong possibility that the potential gold resources on the Busang project...have been overstated because of invalid samples and assaying of those samples," Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said in the statement.
Freeport said in a separate statement analyses of its own drilling results so far "indicate insignificant amounts of gold".
The news caused pandemonium on the Toronto Stock Exchange, which suspended trading in Bre-X shares.

Bre-X shares were hit last week following the mysterious death of its chief geologist Michael de Guzman, who fell out of a helicopter last Wednesday while on his way to the Busang property, and after a news report that the gold reserve in the property might be smaller than estimated by Bre-X.

Sarinastiti said due diligence carried out by Nusamba, Freeport and their Indonesian partners showed that analyses of seven core holes drilled in the Busang II parcel indicated insignificant amounts of gold.
"We are continuing with due diligence work, which remains incomplete," she said. "It will be completed by end of April."
She said representatives of the three parties' technical team handed over all available information on the property to Bre-X officials at a meeting in Jakarta on Wednesday.

"Nusamba, Freeport and their Indonesian partners were informed by Bre-X that based on the recommendations of its independent technical consultants there was a strong possibility that the potential gold resources in the Busang gold project as previously reported by Bre-X had been overstated," she said.
She said Bre-X was undertaking a review that would include drilling additional holes at the Busang II zone, which was previously thought by Bre-X to contain the motherlode.
